identity.name: Rosemary extract
identity.chemical_class: Botanical antioxidant extract rich in phenolic diterpenes (carnosic acid and carnosol)

function.mechanism: Carnosic acid and carnosol inhibit lipid oxidation and scavenge reactive species, slowing rancidity in fat-containing foods.

adi.basis: EFSA opinions reported insufficient data to establish a numerical EFSA ADI; 2018 refined exposure compared intake against the JECFA temporary ADI of 0-0.3 mg/kg bw/day used at that time.

efsa.key_finding: EFSA refined exposure assessment for E392 concluded exposure estimates were conservative and did not indicate a safety concern for reported uses.

adi.basis: Upper bound of JECFA ADI range 0-0.6 mg/kg bw/day (expressed as carnosic acid and carnosol), established after withdrawal of the previous temporary ADI 0-0.3.

concerns.summary: JECFA 2025 identified developmental thyroid-hormone effects in rat pups from maternal exposure studies; BMDL20 was 97 mg/kg bw/day (as carnosic acid plus carnosol), which informed ADI revision.
Mechanistic studies discussed by JECFA indicate CYP-related interaction potential for rosemary constituents; relevance at normal dietary additive exposure remains uncertain.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA did not consider slight child exceedance of the ADI in conservative high-exposure scenarios to represent a safety concern.
EFSA refined exposure assessment reported no safety concern for current reported uses of E392.
Recent human rosemary-extract supplement trials reported generally good short-term tolerability.

adi_exceedance.notes: JECFA 2025 reported high child exposure up to 0.84 mg/kg bw/day versus ADI upper bound 0.6 mg/kg bw/day; adults in cited scenario were up to 0.32 mg/kg bw/day.

risk_assessment.rationale: E392 remains approved/GRAS but has meaningful caveats: child high-end intake can exceed ADI in conservative scenarios and developmental thyroid findings informed ADI setting. Regulators nevertheless judged current assessed uses not to pose a safety concern.
key_factors: EU authorised status with EFSA exposure reassessment
JECFA ADI established at 0-0.6 mg/kg bw/day in 2025
High-end child exposure may exceed ADI in conservative scenarios
Credible developmental thyroid endpoint considered in risk assessment
